chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Mahdi, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
The generous one of good character is under the shelter of Allah; Allah does not leave him alone until He enters him into Paradise.
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any Prophet or Successor except as a generous one.
And there was never anyone from the righteous except as a generous one.
And my father never ceased to advise me with generosity until he passed away.
And he said: 'The one who takes out the complete Zakat from his wealth, and places it in its proper place, will not be questioned: From where did you earn your wealth?'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of generosity and Zakat in Shia tradition according to Imam Musa al-Kazim?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, generosity (sakha') is viewed not merely as charity but as an intrinsic spiritual attribute of the Infallibles, reflecting their divine nature. The hadith emphasizes that consistent, complete Zakat payment serves as a seal of purity for one's wealth, ensuring divine acceptance and shielding the giver from scrutiny regarding the source of their sustenance.
